characters.description: Over the course of the series, he finishes in 1st place four times, and both 2nd place and 3rd place twice, giving him a total of 8 points byNASCARscoring rules and the 9th place in the racers by the end of the series. The Alleged Car: The Turbo Terrific seems to fall to pieces at least once per episode. Alliterative Name:PeterPerfect. Butt-Monkey: He regularly suffers particularly embarrassing accidents or mechanical failures, second only to Dick Dastardly. Catchphrase: Usually "Oh, fiddlesticks!" whenever something goes wrong.

characters.name: Peter Perfect (Driver of the Turbo Terrific)
characters.description: Over the course of the series, he finishes in 1st place four times, and both 2nd place and 3rd place twice, giving him a total of 8 points byNASCARscoring rules and the 9th place in the racers by the end of the series. The Alleged Car: The Turbo Terrific seems to fall to pieces at least once per episode. Alliterative Name:PeterPerfect. Butt-Monkey: He regularly suffers particularly embarrassing accidents or mechanical failures, second only to Dick Dastardly. Catchphrase: Usually "Oh, fiddlesticks!" whenever something goes wrong.

characters.name: Rufus Ruffcut & Sawtooth (Drivers of the Buzzwagon)
characters.description: ByNASCARscoring rules, he does incredibly well through consistently placing in the top 3 finishing spots; with three 1st place finishes,six2nd place finishes, and four 3rd place finishes, he ends up scoring 13 points and thus officially would be considered the 2nd place winner by the end of the series. Accessory-Wearing Cartoon Animal: Sawtooth wears a yellow helmet, a yellow scarf, goggles, and yellow gloves. Alliterative Name:RufusRuffcut. Bamboo Technology: The Buzz Wagon appears to basically be a kart made out of wood with saws for wheels. Big Guy, Little Guy: Rufus and Sawtooth, respectively.

characters.name: Sergeant Blast & Private Meekley (Drivers of the Army Surplus Special)
characters.description: They have one of the most abysmal scoring runs across the course of the series; they do come in 1st place three times, and in 2nd place just the once, but those are the only times they place in the top three in the entirety of the Wacky Races. ByNASCARrules, they thus end up ranking in 10th place by the series end, with a meagre 4 points. Abnormal Ammo: The Surplus Special can shoot different types of ammo, such as bubble gum to stop other racers. Drill Sergeant Nasty: Blast is loud, aggressive, and usually patronizing to Meekley. Dub Name Change:Blast is Sargento Bombarda in Portuguese, Sergent Grosse-Pomme in France, and Gunsō Kakka (軍曹閣下) in Japan.Meekley is Soldat Petit-Pois in France and Shinpei-kun (新兵くん) in Japan.The Mexican dub changed the car's name toSuper Chatarra Especial(Super Junk Special); it counts asCultural Translation, because army surplus is not a thing in Latin America. Blast is Sargento Bombarda in Portuguese, Sergent Grosse-Pomme in France, and Gunsō Kakka (軍曹閣下) in Japan.

characters.name: The Ant Hill Mob (Drivers of the Bulletproof Bomb)
characters.description: A group of seven pint-sized 1920s-style gangsters composing of Clyde, their leader, Ring-A-Ding, Rug Bug Benny, Mac, Danny, Kirby and Willy who race in the Bulletproof Bomb. They are constantly preoccupied with getting caught by the police and are able to use "getaway power", which involves all members, except for Clyde, extending their legs through the bottom of the car and running. ByNASCARracing rules, the Ant Hill Mob manages to score a respectable 11 points and secure themselves 4th place in the final tally of racers, with four 1st place finishes, five 2nd place finishes, and two 3rd place finishes. Bank Robbery: When Dastardly uses a police siren to trick the other racers into stopping, Clyde tells his companions to remember their "alibi" for a bank robbery. Boring, but Practical: Their car is the second most normal out of all the racers after the Turbo Terrific, but they've clinched more high-place finishers than several of the wackier wacky race cars. In fact, out of the four racers who have came in first four times, they have the most second-place victories. Characterization Marches On: In the first episode, they were set up as secondary antagonists after Dick Dastardly, being just as willing to cheat as he was and significantly better at it than him. While they still feared the law over the rest of the series, in subsequent episodes they're just another racing team, and become outright heroes inThe Perils of Penelope Pitstop.

characters.name: Prof. Pat Pending (Driver of the Convert-a-Car)
characters.description: Pat Pending scores three 1st place finishes, two 2nd place finishes, and five 3rd place finishes over the entire series. Per theNASCARrules, that leaves him with 10 points for a 7th place position. Alliterative Name:ProfessorPatPending. Dub Name Change: His name in Spanish is Professor Locovich, with 'Loco' meaning 'Insane'. Dudley Do-Right Stops to Help: He frequently stops and uses his car's inventions to help the other racers, or uses it to deal with whatever trap Dastardly has set up. Unlike Peter Perfect, whom also constantly invokes this trope, Pending rarely ends up troubled or inconvenienced from doing so. Foil: One of two to Dick Dastardly, the other being Peter Perfect. In Pat's case, he goes out of his way to foil Dick Dastardly's attempts at cheating, and while he uses his brains just as much as Dastardly allhisways of doing so are perfectly legal because they're usually part of his car.

characters.name: Penelope Pitstop (Driver of the Compact Pussycat)
characters.description: Penelope has a very swingy record over the course of the Wacky Races; she comes in at 1st place four times, 2nd place twice, and 3rd place five times, but often comes in at 4th place or lower. ByNASCARscoring, she ends up solidly in the middle of the racer rankings at 5th place. Action Girl: In "Idaho A-Go-Go", when lured by Dastardly into a Red Riding Hood trap, Dastardly has Muttley dress as the Wolf, and, as Grandma, asks her to hide in the closet. But she answers the door and gives everyone who answers, including Peter Perfect, the oldFrying Pan of Doom. Affectionate Nickname: She is called "Pretty Penny" for short, especially by Peter Perfect. Alliterative Name:PenelopePitstop. Breakout Character: Like Dastardly and Muttley, Penelope is popular enough to get her ownspin-off series.

characters.name: The Slag Brothers (Drivers of the Bouldermobile)
characters.description: Incredibly, the Slagmobile manages to consistently place in the top 3 finishing spots across the entire Wacky Races the most of any of the contestants; scoring three 1st placeand3rd place finishes, they also achieve a whoppingeight2nd place finishes. ByNASCARrules, that tallies up to 14 points in total, the single highest score of any Wacky Racer... That's right; these guys would officially end the series with the grand prize as the 1st place racing car! Bamboo Technology: Their car is a rock. Don't ask how it works, it just does. Contemporary Caveman: Hairy guys in loincloths, in a stone car. The Dividual: An extreme example considering they're twins who lookandact exactly the same so trying to figure out who's Rock and who's Gravel is ultimately pointless. Dub Name Change: Known as Pietro and Rocco in the Spanish-language dub, which also translated their surname to Macana (a Latin American term for the clubs they wield).

characters.name: The Gruesome Twosome (Drivers of the Creepy Coupe)
characters.description: ByNASCARscoring rules, they officially would be considered the 3rd place winner by the end of the series, with three 1st and 2nd place finishes and six 3rd place finishers, for a total of 12 points. Bigger on the Inside: The small belfry of their car houses a gigantic dragon and sea serpent. Big Guy, Little Guy: Big Gruesome and Little Gruesome, obviously. Captain Ersatz: Of Frankenstein and Dracula, of course. Daywalking Vampire: The sun doesn't seem to be fatal to or even hurtful to Big Gruesome.

characters.name: The Red Max (Driver of the Crimson Haybaler)
characters.description: Over the course of the series, he finishes in both 1st place and 3rd place three times each, as well as finishing in 2nd place four times, giving him a total of 10 points byNASCARscoring rules and the 6th place in the racers by the end of the series. Ace Pilot: Max's appearance and vehicle are themed on World War I fighter pilots and post-WWI barnstormers, and uses a lot of aviation slang and terminology in his dialogue. Butt-Monkey: Possibly the third worst example after Dick Dastardly (who usually brings it on himself) and Peter Perfect, as the Haybailer's limited flight capabilities make it prime fodder for Michael Maltese'sGravity Is a Harsh Mistressgags. Dub Name Change: Known as Baron Hans Fritz in the Spanish-language dub. The Crimson Haybaler was renamed as the Stuka Rakuda. Family-Friendly Firearms: In the Dreamcast/PS2game, the Haybailer's machine gun actually fires paintballs, and the car can also directly launch its propeller as a homing projectile.

characters.name: Lazy Luke & Blubber Bear (Drivers of the Arkansas Chuggabug)
characters.description: Over the course of the series, he finishes in both 1st place and 3rd place four times each, as well as 2nd place just once, giving him a total of 9 points byNASCARscoring rules and the 9th place in the racers by the end of the series. Accessory-Wearing Cartoon Animal: Blubber wears a blue helmet with goggles and a green scarf. Alliterative Name:LazyLuke.BlubberBear. Bamboo Technology: Not quite as bad as the Slag Brothers or Rufus Ruffcut, but their car is powered by a steam boiler made out of an old-fashioned potbellied stove. One episode reveals that their engine is assisted by a squirrel on an exercise wheel. Beary Funny: Blubber may be a bear, but he's hardly scary.

characters.name: Dick Dastardly & Muttley (Drivers of the Mean Machine)
characters.description: Of course, as the series' designated villain, byNASCARrules, Dick Dastardly finishes the Wacky Races ranked in atdead last, with 0 points; he never gets a single 1st, 2nd or 3rd place finish in the series. In fact, he almost always finishes dead last in the race, typically because heDNFs, and if he doesn't finish dead last,somethingwill happen to disqualify him. Accessory-Wearing Cartoon Animal: Muttley wears a red collar. Alliterative Name:DickDastardly. Angrish: When not snickering, Muttley's dialogue mainly consists of muttered grumbling such as "Sassarassafrassa..." The Bad Guy Wins: Never in the show, but in other media.In the video games where they’re playable, you can finally break their losing streak and have them win a race. The Amiga game fits this the best, as your end goal is for them to win, and the ending even comments that they won for the first time ever.They also won a few times in the tie in comics. Dastardly even got a trophy, which he used to soak his feet.Finally, they did win a few times in other appearances outside the show, though there was almost always a catch to make sure the audience didn’t feel too cheated that they won.

characters.name: Dick Dastardly
characters.description: The racer of the Mean Machine. Known for his attempts at cheating, the keyword beingattempts. Adaptational Wimp: The original Dick Dastardly was far from manly or capable, but this version is considerably wimpier and prone to complaining over action. Alliterative Name: Retained from the original series. Also applies to his supervillain persona, thePurplePuppeteer in "Super Wacky". Brilliant, but Lazy: He's a very competent and skilled racer constantly wrecking his own efforts with various complex traps and schemes. He admits in "Do Over Dastardly" that he'd rather win through cheating because it's just more fun, whereas trying to apply himself to win fairly would be like work. Catchphrase:As in the original series, "Drat, drat and double drat!", or somevariation."Muttley, this is all your fault!", derived from his appearances inYogi’s Treasure Hunt.

characters.name: Muttley
characters.description: Dastardly's not-so-loyal lackey. Alliterative Name: His supervillain persona, theSonicSnicker in "Super Wacky". Angrish: "Rassamfrassamrassam" Aw, Look! They Really Do Love Each Other: Towards Dastardly, as unlikely as it seems."Peter Imperfect": He is deeply affected by Dastardly's change of personality, even letting out aHowl of Sorrow. Penelope later points out that no one wanted Dastardly back to normal more than Muttley did."Muttleys Are Forever": Muttleysurrenders to Dr. Doomsdoctor rather than letting Dastardly be blown up (despite having been fired mere moments earlier) and opts to stay by Dastardly's side after the world is saved. "Peter Imperfect": He is deeply affected by Dastardly's change of personality, even letting out aHowl of Sorrow. Penelope later points out that no one wanted Dastardly back to normal more than Muttley did.

characters.name: Peter Perfect
characters.description: The racer of the Turbo Terrific who does his best to be the perfect racer and role model. His looks don’t quite fit his intelligence, though. Alliterative Name: Retained from the original series. All-Loving Hero: Consistently nice and charitable to everyone, even Dastardly. His reputation as this is why the owner has him do so many endorsements and promotional appearances. Attention Whore: When Peter thinks Dick is ignoring him, he becomes distraught and admits that he needs to be the center of attention. Berserk Button: Spends "Off Track" getting hassled by his smug older brother, but when Paul starts insulting the other racers, Peter finally asserts himself.

characters.name: Penelope Pitstop
characters.description: The southern belle racer who's every fanboy's dream. Action Girl: Penelope takes part in a lot of athletic events in her spare time; "Peter 2.0" opens with a scene of her casually skydiving. Adaptational Curves: She has a more curvy appearance compared to her relatively slimmer look in the original show andThe Perils of Penelope Pitstop. Adaptation Personality Change: Penelope is more athletic, quick-witted, and focused on racing than she was in the original series. All Girls Like Ponies: In one scene of "Guru My Dreams", Penelope dreams she's riding a unicorn.

characters.name: I.Q. Ickly
characters.description: Young boy genius racer with a talking, robotic car and all sorts of gadgets up his sleeves. Child Prodigy: I.Q.'s the type of person who knows all the digits of pi off the top of his head and constantly gets invitations to show off his tech to the world. Cool Car: Cara, complete with tech and A.I. Does Not Drive: Yes, in a show about racing, he technically doesn't drive, because he's just a kid. Instead his car drives itself while he issues orders. When in once episodethe characters start to change bodieshe immediately loses control of Peter Perfect's car after admitting he doesn't actually know how to drive. Gadgeteer Genius: For starters, he once invented a 30-second time machine.

characters.name: The Gruesome Twosome
characters.description: The renamed brother duo, who drive the monster truck known as the Doombuggy. Big Guy, Little Guy: Tiny'sheadis bigger than Bella's whole body. Dark Is Not Evil: They're macabre monsters, but generally friendly with the other racers when not competing. Daywalking Vampire: Bella doesn't seem to have any trouble in the sunlight. The Ditz: Tiny, complete withHulk Speak.

characters.name: Pandora Pitstop
characters.description: Penelope'sEvil Twin, who like Dastardly, is willing to cheat to win, but unlike him, she knows how to pull off underhanded tactics. Beauty Is Bad: Penelope's twin sister who'salsogood-looking (even playing as a siren in one episode) but is much more villainous. Distaff Counterpart: To Dick Dastardly, being a purple-clad racer who is willing to cheat to gain victory. Evil Brunette Twin: A stark contrast from her Goody two-shoes, blonde twin sister Penelope. Evil Twin: And younger - by 12 seconds.

characters.name: Scrappy-Doo
characters.description: Freudian Excuse: He's shown to take pleasure in pranking Dastardly (without Dastardly realizing it), but it's also shown that the omniscient network executives have a bone to pick with him. The Gadfly: This version of Scrappy's one real defining characteristic is enjoying screwing with Dastardly. Rebellious Spirit: If one gets the unenviable number one spot on the Network's black list, one has to participate in a series of "wholesome" programming in order to regain their position. Scrappy went off the grid, and switched spots with Dick. Small Role, Big Impact:In Uncle Dickie's Happy Funshine Hour, it's shown thatsomeoneswitched the listings with Dastardly to makehimnumber two. Said someone has paws like Scrappy. Tragic Villain: We see first and in "Uncle Dickie" how disastrous it is for whoever is at the top of the Exec's naughty list. Even being at number two must have felt like a breather. The poor guy only dared move up to number two, and that was after being at the top of the naughty list foryears.

characters.name: The Hooded Claw
characters.description: This recurring villain who originated inThe Perils of Penelope Pitstopwants nothing but to take Dastardly down a notch and realize the errors of his ways. Big Bad Wannabe: Gets taken down by Dastardly in all his appearances, despite wanting to pose as a legitimate threat to the racers. Hypocrite: The argument he makes against Dastardly in "The Trial of Dick Dastardly" states that his show should be cancelled because ofhis gratuitous slapstick not being suitable for the viewing audience. A few episodes later in "From Dast to Worse", Hooded Claw spends the entire episode trying to thwart his plans despite making a case against it earlier. Poor Man's Substitute: In-universe, no matter how hard he tries to differentiate himself, he’s seen as this to Dastardly. Gets lampshaded in "Unlicensed to Drive" when the driving teacher believes that Dastardly is the Hooded Claw.

characters.name: Brick Crashman
characters.description: The narrator of the Wacky Races. Ascended Extra: The original series had anInteractive Narrator; in this version, the narrator is a new character. Deadline News: He doesn't die, but it increasingly becomes aRunning Gagthat the events of each episode injure orscrew him overduring his broadcasts. Mr. Exposition: Some of the alternate universe episodes open up with him discussing the time period the episode takes place in. Token Minority: He is the only black character in the show.

characters.name: Sunny Manners
characters.description: An old lady in charge of standards & practices for the show. Prone to calling out violence whenever she sees it and restraining the racers. Biting-the-Hand Humor: One of the weapons she offers the racers in "Racer Roundup" isa foam boomerang. Double Standard: Her restrictions are built on this. She can allow the racers tokill a robot with a bunnybut as soon as a racer isn’t wearing their seatbelt, the gloves are off. Media Watchdog: Parodied. As one of the people in charge of the show, she takes her job as a censor a bit too far and forces the racers into unfavorable situations. Strawman Has a Point:In-Universe. She admits, along with the other racers, that letting Dastardly write an episode of the show was an awful idea in "I, Racecar".
